finding_key: packages/backend/src/main.ts::raw-body capture keys off an exact `req.url` string match while express routes the same endpoint far more leniently — any trailing slash, case difference, duplicated slash or path prefix makes every webhook 401 and silently disables the feature
evidence: The code at packages/backend/src/main.ts:51 does an exact equality check `req.url?.split('?', 1)[0] === '/internal/yorkie/events'`, while Nest's Express adapter routes with the defaults `caseSensitive: false` and `strict: false`, so `/internal/yorkie/events/` or `/Internal/Yorkie/Events` still reaches `YorkieEventController.handleEvent` but with `rawBody` unset, and yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49 then throws `UnauthorizedException('Missing webhook signature')` — the coupling described is genuinely brittle. The claim's supporting detail is also accurate that no test covers the capture: test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts `applyGlobalBootstrap` installs only the ValidationPipe, not the bodyParser verify hook. Two sub-points are shaky: a duplicated slash (`//internal/...`) would generally not match the Express route at all (404, not a silent 401), and there is no `setGlobalPrefix` today so the "path prefix" case is hypothetical; also the 401 is not entirely silent since pino logs 4xx at warn. Net: a real latent fragility that only bites if the ops-registered webhook URL differs in case/trailing slash from the documented one (docs/design/documents-last-modified.md ops block), which makes it a robustness/minor issue rather than a defect on the happy path.
